may_be_looking_for: People with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) as defined by at least 4 criteria from the American Rheumatism Association
Those with membranous lupus nephropathy showing 2 or more grams of protein in urine per day, without infection or other kidney disease
People whose kidney biopsy shows typical membranous lupus nephropathy with immune deposits mainly under the lining of kidney filters
may_exclude_people_who: Have taken cytotoxic drugs or cyclosporin A for more than 2 weeks in the 10 weeks before starting the study
patient_summary: This study looked at different combinations of immunosuppressive drugs for people with membranous lupus nephropathy, a kidney condition linked to lupus. The goal was to see if these drugs could reduce protein in the urine and prevent kidney failure. Participants were followed for 12 months.
patient_title: Study of Drug Therapy for Membranous Lupus Nephropathy
questions_to_ask_clinician: What tests will be done before and during the study?
How will I be assigned to a treatment group?
What are the possible side effects of the medications used in this study?
Will I need to stay in the hospital during the study?
What kind of follow-up will I need after the study ends?
uncertainty_notes: This study was completed, but individual results may differ. The study outcomes and safety of these drug combinations are not guaranteed.
The study only included people with specific medical histories, so findings may not apply to everyone with lupus nephropathy.
what_researchers_are_studying: The researchers studied how well different combinations of immunosuppressive medications (prednisone, cyclophosphamide, and cyclosporin A) work over 12 months to lower protein levels in urine and protect kidney function in people with membranous lupus nephropathy.
